title: 12. Numeracy & Number Systems: Multi-Digit Subtraction with Regrouping
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Subtract two two-digit whole numbers with regrouping in the ones place.
questions.question: What is \(52-27\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract the ones digits: \(2\) is less than \(7\), so regroup \(1\) ten from the tens place. Then \(12-7=5\) in the ones place. The tens place becomes \(4\), and \(4-2=2\). Therefore, \(52-27=25\).
questions.hint: Regroup \(1\) ten from the tens place when the ones digit is too small to subtract from.

questions.learningObjective: Subtract two two-digit whole numbers with regrouping in the ones place.
questions.question: What is \(63-28\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract the ones digits: \(3\) is less than \(8\), so regroup \(1\) ten. Then \(13-8=5\) in the ones place. The tens place becomes \(5\), and \(5-2=3\). Therefore, \(63-28=35\).
questions.hint: After regrouping, subtract the ones digits first, then subtract the tens digits.

questions.learningObjective: Subtract two two-digit whole numbers with regrouping in the ones place.
questions.question: What is \(71-46\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract the ones digits: \(1\) is less than \(6\), so regroup \(1\) ten. Then \(11-6=5\) in the ones place. The tens place becomes \(6\), and \(6-4=2\). Therefore, \(71-46=25\).
questions.hint: Regroup from the tens place, then subtract each column from right to left.

questions.learningObjective: Subtract a three-digit whole number from another three-digit whole number with regrouping.
questions.question: What is \(342-158\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract the ones digits: \(2\) is less than \(8\), so regroup \(1\) ten. Then \(12-8=4\). The tens place becomes \(3\), and \(3\) is less than \(5\), so regroup \(1\) hundred. Then \(13-5=8\). The hundreds place becomes \(2\), and \(2-1=1\). Therefore, \(342-158=184\).
questions.hint: Regroup whenever a digit in the top number is smaller than the digit below it.

questions.learningObjective: Subtract a three-digit whole number from a three-digit number involving regrouping across zero.
questions.question: What is \(506-278\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract the ones digits: \(6\) is less than \(8\). Since the tens digit is \(0\), regroup \(1\) hundred from the hundreds place. This gives \(10\) tens, then regroup \(1\) ten to the ones place. The ones become \(16\), and \(16-8=8\). The tens become \(9\), and \(9-7=2\). The hundreds become \(4\), and \(4-2=2\). Therefore, \(506-278=228\).
questions.hint: When a zero digit blocks regrouping, regroup from the next nonzero place to its left.

questions.learningObjective: Subtract a three-digit whole number from another three-digit whole number with regrouping in multiple places.
questions.question: What is \(723-456\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract the ones digits: \(3\) is less than \(6\), so regroup \(1\) ten. Then \(13-6=7\). The tens place becomes \(1\), and \(1\) is less than \(5\), so regroup \(1\) hundred. Then \(11-5=6\). The hundreds place becomes \(6\), and \(6-4=2\). Therefore, \(723-456=267\).
questions.hint: Work from right to left and regroup whenever the top digit is smaller.

questions.learningObjective: Subtract a four-digit whole number from a four-digit number involving regrouping across zeros.
questions.question: What is \(4{,}002-1{,}568\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract the ones digits: \(2\) is less than \(8\). Regroup across the zeros: \(4{,}002\) becomes \(3\) thousands, \(9\) hundreds, \(9\) tens, and \(12\) ones. Then \(12-8=4\). Subtract the tens: \(9-6=3\). Subtract the hundreds: \(9-5=4\). Subtract the thousands: \(3-1=2\). Therefore, \(4{,}002-1{,}568=2{,}434\).
questions.hint: Regroup step by step through the zeros before subtracting each column.

questions.learningObjective: Subtract a four-digit whole number from another four-digit whole number with regrouping across zero.
questions.question: What is \(6{,}305-2{,}478\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract the ones digits: \(5\) is less than \(8\). Since the tens digit is \(0\), regroup \(1\) hundred from the hundreds place. This gives \(10\) tens, then regroup \(1\) ten to the ones place. The ones become \(15\), and \(15-8=7\). The tens become \(9\), and \(9-7=2\). The hundreds become \(2\), and \(2\) is less than \(4\), so regroup \(1\) thousand. Then \(12-4=8\). The thousands become \(5\), and \(5-2=3\). Therefore, \(6{,}305-2{,}478=3{,}827\).
questions.hint: Regroup from the hundreds place to the tens place, then from the thousands place to the hundreds place if needed.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a word problem by subtracting a four-digit whole number with regrouping.
questions.question: A library had \(5{,}000\) books. Then \(1{,}236\) books were borrowed. How many books remain in the library?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of borrowed books from the original total: \(5{,}000-1{,}236\). Regroup across the zeros: \(5{,}000\) becomes \(4\) thousands, \(9\) hundreds, \(9\) tens, and \(10\) ones. Then \(10-6=4\), \(9-3=6\), \(9-2=7\), and \(4-1=3\). Therefore, \(5{,}000-1{,}236=3{,}764\) books.
questions.hint: Identify the total and the amount removed, then subtract using regrouping across zeros.

questions.learningObjective: Subtract a four-digit whole number from a four-digit number with regrouping across multiple zeros.
questions.question: What is \(9{,}000-3{,}468\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract the ones digits: \(0\) is less than \(8\). Regroup across the zeros: \(9{,}000\) becomes \(8\) thousands, \(9\) hundreds, \(9\) tens, and \(10\) ones. Then \(10-8=2\). Subtract the tens: \(9-6=3\). Subtract the hundreds: \(9-4=5\). Subtract the thousands: \(8-3=5\). Therefore, \(9{,}000-3{,}468=5{,}532\).
questions.hint: Start with the ones place. When zeros block regrouping, regroup from the nearest nonzero place to the left and pass the regrouping through each zero.
